# jcode

High-performance coding agents.
Run more agents with less RAM for your multi-agent development workflow.

[Website](https://jcode.sh) · [Docs](https://jcode.sh/docs) · [SDK](https://jcode.sh/sdk) · [Benchmarks](https://jcode.sh/bench) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [Install](#installation) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
## Screenshots [Browse the interactive gallery on jcode.sh](https://jcode.sh/#screenshots).

Info widgets
## Installation
```bash # macOS & Linux curl -fsSL https://jcode.sh/install | bash ``` [Windows installation instructions](https://jcode.sh/docs#install).

aiSummary.oneLiner: A RAM-efficient terminal harness for running intelligent AI coding agents like Claude and OpenAI models locally.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: jcode is a lightweight command-line interface and terminal harness designed to run AI coding agents with extreme memory efficiency. Built in Rust, it connects to advanced large language models such as Claude and OpenAI via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to assist with software development tasks directly in the terminal. It provides a structured environment where agents can read codebases, execute commands, and suggest changes without consuming excessive system resources. The tool aims to offer the most intelligent coding assistance while maintaining a minimal memory footprint.
keyFeatures: High RAM efficiency: Built in Rust to ensure the harness consumes minimal memory while running complex agents.
Model integrations: Connects natively with leading LLMs including Claude and OpenAI models.
Terminal-native UI: Provides a fully featured text-based interface for interacting with agents directly in your shell.
MCP support: Implements the Model Context Protocol to give agents standardized access to local tools and context.
Extensible SDK: Offers an SDK for developers to build custom integrations and benchmarks.

releases.name: v0.98.1
releases.body:
**Faster idle sessions and richer responses**

### Highlights

- Reduce idle CPU and disk reads in repositories with many untracked files
- Share model catalog processing across equivalent clients while keeping usage and account state fresh
- Allow Desktop-capable clients to receive Markdown responses through the new user_response tool

### Improvements

- Show compact context usage before and after compaction
- Open the resume picker immediately while session scanning continues in the background
- Disable automatic memory recall while retaining explicit memory search
- Display large recorded token and cost summaries compactly

### Fixes

- Recover browser handoffs from runtime provider failures using direct browser actions
- Restore Windows companion connections over named pipes
- Expose global user-session connection presence to SDK clients
- Keep worker emoji placement consistent in the swarm status strip

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode/compare/v0.97.0...v0.98.1

releases.name: v0.97.0
releases.body:
### Highlights

- Use custom HTTP JSON search providers with configurable authentication, result mapping, and fallback engines
- Rust and TypeScript SDK clients can invoke native runtime commands and transfer sessions without turning commands into agent prompts

### Improvements

- Dismiss side panels directly from the TUI, and keep routine system notices on a compact single line
- Default opt-out usage telemetry can now include the active Anthropic or OpenAI OAuth account email when the matching server rollout is available, with a conditional one-time TUI notice, 90-day retention, and collection controls in /telemetry

### Fixes

- Azure agent turns use the Responses API with correct route selection, explicit reasoning settings, and more reliable tool-call and retry handling
- Anthropic model catalog requests include the required authentication headers
- Browser handoff failures preserve reconnect timeout diagnostics
- Empty math no longer triggers LaTeX rendering, and repeated fallback failures avoid duplicate logging

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode/compare/v0.96.0...v0.97.0

releases.name: v0.96.0
releases.body:
### Highlights

- Connect to remote MCP servers over HTTP or SSE, including OAuth sign-in and command-line management
- Choose saved OAuth accounts per session from the model and login pickers, with email labels and cancelable account-switch countdowns
- SDK clients can organize sessions into collections and attach hidden reminders to individual turns

### Improvements

- Swarm messages use compact, expandable one-row previews, while the activity dock shows session icons and each worker's current todo step
- Pinned todos span the full terminal width
- The /reset usage limits claude command supports resetting Claude session limits
- Prompts and pokes appear in every window attached to a session
- New-model usage costs receive estimates before published pricing becomes available

### Fixes

- The first pinned todo update no longer hides the original session prompt, and hidden todo updates preserve transcript cache boundaries
- OpenAI native web citations render source links reliably without losing links already shown
- Provider failover honors account pools and model preferences, rotates rejected OAuth accounts, and stops retrying permanently rejected sessions
- Stale Anthropic usage

releases.name: v0.95.0
releases.body:
### Highlights

- OpenCode Go models, including grok-4.7 and gpt-6-luna, now route over the Responses API
- Hooks expose turn-end token usage, and turn_start/turn_end now fire for one-shot jcode run turns
- /agents supports per-session worker model overrides

### Improvements

- /resume can open scoped to the current project when display.resume_project_scope is enabled
- Swarm gains a stalled-worker watchdog, and headless run --socket sessions can join swarms
- The macOS menu bar helper uses a stable signing identity, draws the streaming icon green, and can be turned off with [menubar] enabled = false
- Inline images fit their reserved box and the info widget hugs its content
- Command risk assessment now inspects commands inside $(...), backticks, and heredocs
- SDK-launched private instances no longer auto-update mid-session and give shorter, more accurate connect errors

### Fixes

- Ctrl/Alt/Cmd shortcuts work on the Korean 2-Set input source
- The terminal keyboard protocol and TUI modes are restored when jcode exits on a signal
- Rate-limit and provider reconnect auto-resumes are bounded instead of retrying indefinitely
- OpenAI streams recover faster from stalls and OAuth to

releases.name: v0.94.0
releases.body:
**Queued commands**

### Highlights

- Ctrl+Enter queues slash and ! commands to run after the current turn, and /clear drops anything still queued
- Alt+G opens the project's git commit log, and diff cycling moves to /diff
- Harness API clients can observe and cancel messages sent mid-turn

### Improvements

- The startup frame settles immediately instead of popping in over about 200ms, with session facts shown on the first frame
- The Overview widget stays visible after startup
- Onboarding is cleaner: side-by-side start choice, no starter prompt cards, and the home directory is labeled '~ (home)'
- Onboarding detects accounts you are signed in with in Cursor, other AI tools, and stored Jcode agent logins
- Restored transcripts and the session picker preview no longer show a redundant 'tool:' summary line

### Fixes

- Escaped single-word brackets like \[workspace\] are no longer rendered as display math
- Onboarding's Import option no longer commits when pressing Enter, and toggling preview no longer flickers the screen
- Sleep inhibition keeps its lock across refreshes and retries after helper failures

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode/compare/v0.93.0...v0.

jcode performance demonstration

Swarm

Spawn two or more agents in the same repo, and they will automatically be managed by the server to allow native collaboration. When agent A edits a file that agent B has read (code shifting under its feet), the server notifies agent B. Agent B can ignore it if it is not relevant, or it can check the diff to make sure that it doesn't conflict. Each agent has messaging abilities, capable of DMing just one agent, broadcasting to all other agents hosted by the server, or just agents working in that repo. This allows you to spawn multiple sessions in the same repo, and have all conflicts automatically resolved.

jcode swarm demonstration

Agents are also able to spawn their own swarms autonomously. They have a swarm tool which allows them to spawn in their own teamates to accomplish tasks in parallel. Doing so turns the main agent into a coordinator and the spawned agents into workers. Groups of agents, their messaging channels, their completion statuses, etc are all automatically managed. This can be done headlessly or headed.

Swarm modes keep root reasoning separate from worker effort. Configure each mode in ~/.jcode/config.toml:

[agents]
swarm_root_effort = "low"        # /effort swarm
swarm_deep_root_effort = "high"  # /effort swarm-deep

Both default to max. Accepted levels are none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, and max, mapped to the provider's supported range. The effort switcher shows the configured root level. These settings do not change worker swarm_effort. Environment overrides are JCODE_SWARM_ROOT_EFFORT and JCODE_SWARM_DEEP_ROOT_EFFORT.

OAuth and Providers

Supports a wide range of providers, including Claude OAuth and OpenAI Codex OAuth.

Customizability / Self-Dev

Jcode is inventing a new form of customizability. One that doesn't limit you to what a plugin or extension can do. Tell your jcode agent to enter self dev mode, and it will start modifying its own source code. Jcode is optimized to iterate on itself. There is significant infrastructure around self development, which allows it to edit, build, and test its own source code, then reload its own binary and continue work in your (potentially many) sessions, fully automatically.

It is recommended that you use a frontier model for this. The jcode codebase is not a simple one, and weaker models can make subtle, breaking changes. GPT 5.5 or the latest available frontier model works well.

Misc.

The devil is in the details. There are many undocumented optimizations and niceties that jcode implements. Some examples:

Anthropic's Claude cache goes cold after 5 minutes. If you initiate Claude after these 5 minutes, you have a cache miss, potentially costing you lots of tokens. The ui warns you when the cache went cold, and notfies you if there was an unexpected cache miss.

jcode comes with instructions on how to set up Firefox Agent Bridge. Ask you agent to set it up, and then you will have browser automation in jcode as well.

Agent grep is a grep tool I made for the jcode agent. It adds file structure information (ie the list of functions, their displacement, etc) to the grep return, so that the agent can infer more of what the file doesn without actually reading the file. It also implements a harness-level integration that adaptively truncates returns based on what the agent has already seen. This saves on context a lot.

Inputs are by default interleaved with the working agent. It sends the input as soon as it safely can without breaking the KV cache. Submit with shift enter instead, and it will send a queue send, and wait for the agent to fully finish its turn before sending.

Resume sessions from different harnesses. Claude code broke on you? Resume the session from jcode and continue where you left off. Session resume is supported for codex, claude code, opencode, and pi.

Skills are not all loaded on startup. The conversation is embedded as a semantic vector, and will automatically inject a skill if there is an embedding hit similar to memories. The agent has a skill tool for you to manually activate a skill at anytime. You may also activate via slash commands.

Browser Automation

The built-in browser tool lets agents navigate pages, fill forms, upload files, and capture screenshots through Firefox Agent Bridge. Ask your agent to set it up and handle browser tasks directly.

See Browser Provider Protocol for details.
